# Fix registry

**Generated by `tools/build-fix-registry.py` - do not edit by hand.**

Rebuilt from git history and the contents of `fork-fix-tests/`, because a
hand-kept list drifts: the Fixed table in `UPSTREAM_TRIAGE.md` was eight entries
behind its own commits when this was written, and several commit messages cite
test directories that have never existed. Nothing here is typed in by hand, so
nothing here can claim a test that is not on disk.

- **84 issues** with at least one fix commit
- **48** have a test artifact in `fork-fix-tests/`
- **36** do not - the fix is asserted by its commit message only
- **20** fix commits carry no issue number (defects found in passing)

A row here means a commit exists. It does **not** mean the fix was verified;
that is what the Test column is for. See the verification status section of
`UPSTREAM_TRIAGE.md` for why that distinction is drawn so sharply.

## Listed as fixed, but no commit claims them

The work is in the tree; nothing ties it to the issue. A commit can claim
an issue three ways - in its subject, as `#NNNN:` opening a body line, or
as `Upstream report: ONLYOFFICE/DesktopEditors#NNNN`. These use none of
them, usually because one commit closed several duplicate reports and
named only the first.
